newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka Banka may shelve Eurobond issue - source.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka Banka may shelve Eurobond issue - source.

text.p: Croatia's Zagrebacka Banka may shelve plans to issue Eurobonds this spring because of a good chance to tap the syndicated loan market at better terms, a well informed source said on Tuesday.
It has received offers by a syndicate of five major foreign banks to arrange a three-year 300 million mark credit at 50 basis points over Libor, the source told Reuters.
Zagrebacka originally aimed to raise the same amount on the Eurobond market and channel it into credits for its clients.
Union Bank of Switzerland and Salomon Brothers were said to have been engaged to arrange the issue.
Two international agencies recently gave the bank long- and short-term investment grade ratings, equal to the sovereign debt rating Croatia won in January.
But a generally weaker investor interest for Eurobonds, including the $250 million raised by the government, caused Zagrebacka to reconsider its plans.

"There is no question whether (its issue) would be sold, but it might turn out to be more expensive than the bank first thought," the source said. "Somebody bungled Croatian bonds and yield has slumped," he added, referring to the sovereign issue.
Croatia is paying annual interest of seven percent over five years for its first Eurobond issue, priced at 80 basis points over U.S. treasuries.
